routes.description: Establish ordinary stance-independent moral objectivity, support an ontology of normative facts through deliberative indispensability, and show that rival-package challenges neither create a genuine deliberative gap nor impose a distinctive comparative liability on realism.
routes.successCriteria: The route succeeds if stance-independent normative facts remain a justified account of ordinary moral objectivity, an agent's first-person conclusion about what ought to be done can settle deliberation, and iterative rival-package objections do not supply a burden-defeating reason to reject realism.

motionBridge.description: Connect stance-independent normative truth to action by requiring that a first-person conclusion about what ought to be done normally completes deliberation without an additional allegiance decision.

centralBridges.description: Explain why ordinary moral claims presuppose independence from preferences and conventions and why this supports realist normative facts.
Supply an affirmative basis for normative facts by showing their indispensable role in deliberation and practical reasoning.
Answer the privilege regress by explaining why iteration does not establish a genuine further normative question or a distinctive objection to realism.
Compare theories by their treatment of central deliberative practice while assigning proportionate significance to rare reflective anomalies.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Identify the additional commitments required for a non-cognitivist alternative to preserve ordinary claims of moral objectivity.
Explain when justified confidence can terminate iterative philosophical challenges without requiring persuasion of every skeptical or confused agent.

routes.description: Distinguish mind-independent moral properties from action-settling objectivity, demonstrate that metaphysical privilege cannot determine allegiance among rival normative packages, and develop an attitude-centered alternative that closes the remaining gap between normative representation and decision.
routes.successCriteria: The route succeeds if rival stance-independent packages leave an intelligible further question about what to do, neither nonnormative nor normative privilege resolves that question without regress, and an alternative account can connect normative judgment to action more directly than realist facts alone.

motionBridge.description: Show that the existence and recognition of stance-independent normative facts can leave unresolved which rival normative package an agent should follow in acting.

centralBridges.description: Establish that nonnormative metaphysical privilege is practically inert while normative privilege recreates the rival-package question at a higher level.
Use informed reflective disputes to show that knowledge of normative or logical facts need not non-causally settle an agent's deliberation.
Explain how deciding, prescribing, or adopting an action-directed attitude can exclude incompatible actions without requiring allegiance among rival truth-apt properties.
Defend the evidential importance of foundational anomalies even when they are rare, abstract, or do not amount to a classical contradiction.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Show how an attitude-centered alternative might avoid dependence on the full semantic machinery associated with standard expressivism.
Separate denial of true contradictions from questions about legitimate consequence relations and the comparative severity of theoretical costs.

sections.title: Ordinary objectivity and the realist foundation
sections.rationale: This issue fixes what stance independence amounts to, whether ordinary moral discourse supports robust realist facts, and whether deliberative indispensability supplies an affirmative basis for their ontology.

sections.title: Rival normative packages and metaphysical privilege
sections.rationale: This is the governing clash over whether metaphysical privilege can identify the action-guiding normative package or instead becomes practically inert or recursively contested.

sections.title: Non-cognitivism as a comparative alternative
sections.rationale: This issue tests whether an attitude-centered account can connect normative judgment with decision while still accommodating the ordinary objectivity that motivates realism.

sections.title: First-person deliberation and reflective counterexamples
sections.rationale: This issue determines whether concluding that one ought to act normally settles deliberation and whether rare, informed disputes reveal a genuine residual choice among normative standards.

sections.title: Theoretical costs, anomalies, and legitimate stopping points
sections.rationale: This issue governs how much weight to assign explanatory anomalies, contradictions, exceptional cases, and iterative skeptical challenges when comparing accounts of normative objectivity.
